title: Design a Library Management System (OOD)
prompt: Design a library management system. Members search a catalog and borrow physical books; each book has multiple copies; loans have due dates and late fines; a member can place a hold on a copy that is currently checked out and be notified when one frees up. Model the classes, relationships, the copy/loan lifecycle, and the key APIs. Sketch the class diagram.
blurb: A CRUD-shaped OOD with real depth — the Book vs BookCopy distinction, a loan/hold state machine, fines, and notifications.

rubric.label: Requirements clarification
rubric.description: Clarifies multiple copies per title, loan period and limits, fines, holds/reservations, and notification before designing.

rubric.label: Core entities
rubric.description: Distinguishes Book (title/metadata) from BookCopy (physical item); identifies Member, Loan, Hold/Reservation, Catalog, Fine.

rubric.label: Class design
rubric.description: Book vs BookCopy modeled correctly, Loan links member+copy+dates, Account/Member holds limits and fines; no conflation of title and item.

rubric.label: Relationships
rubric.description: Book has-many BookCopy; Member has-many Loan; Hold references a Book/BookCopy and a Member; correct multiplicities.

rubric.label: State machine
rubric.description: BookCopy lifecycle (AVAILABLE/LOANED/ON_HOLD/LOST) and Loan lifecycle (ACTIVE/RETURNED/OVERDUE) with clean transitions.

rubric.label: Design patterns
rubric.description: Observer for hold notifications, Strategy for fine calculation, Factory/Repository for catalog access; each justified.

rubric.label: API methods
rubric.description: search, checkout, returnBook, placeHold, cancelHold, renew, payFine; sensible signatures and error cases.

rubric.label: Extensibility
rubric.description: New item types (DVDs, e-books), different fine policies, membership tiers, or reservation rules slot in cleanly.

rubric.label: Edge cases
rubric.description: All copies out, loan limit reached, overdue blocking new loans, hold queue ordering, lost book, double-return.

rubric.label: Concurrency
rubric.description: Two members checking out the last copy or claiming a freed hold simultaneously; atomic copy allocation and hold fulfillment.

rubric.label: Communication
rubric.description: Drives requirements, keeps the class diagram legible, and reasons about the copy/loan/hold interplay.

functional_requirements: Search the catalog by title, author, subject, or ISBN
Track multiple physical copies per book title
Check out a copy to a member with a due date; enforce per-member loan limits
Return a copy; compute and record late fines
Place/cancel a hold on a title when all copies are out; notify the member when a copy frees
Renew a loan if no one is waiting; pay fines
nonfunctional_requirements: No double-loan of a single physical copy
Fair hold queue (FIFO) and reliable notification on availability
Extensible to new item types and fine/membership policies
Thread-safe copy allocation and hold fulfillment
clarifying_questions: Multiple copies per title? Do members borrow a title or a specific copy?
Loan period, max concurrent loans per member, and renewal rules?
Fine policy — flat per day, tiered, capped? Do overdue fines block new checkouts?
Holds/reservations — FIFO queue? How is the member notified (email/SMS)?
Do we handle non-book items (DVDs, e-books) now or later?
What happens to a lost copy — fine + remove from circulation?

core_classes.name: Library
core_classes.responsibility: Aggregate root / facade: exposes search, checkout, return, hold; coordinates catalog, members, and policies.

core_classes.name: Book
core_classes.responsibility: Title-level metadata (bibliographic record); NOT a physical item.

core_classes.name: BookCopy
core_classes.responsibility: A single physical item with its own barcode and lifecycle state.

core_classes.name: Member / Account
core_classes.responsibility: A borrower: active loans, fines owed, membership limits.

core_classes.name: Loan
core_classes.responsibility: Links a member to a borrowed copy with issue/due dates; computes overdue status.

core_classes.name: Hold / Reservation
core_classes.responsibility: A member's place in the waiting queue for a title; fulfilled when a copy frees.

core_classes.name: Catalog / BookRepository
core_classes.responsibility: Indexes books for fast search and looks up copies.

core_classes.name: NotificationObserver (interface)
core_classes.responsibility: Notifies a member when a held copy becomes available.

relationships: Book has-many BookCopy (composition) — the core distinction: title vs physical item
Member has-many Loan (aggregation of active loans)
Loan associates one Member with one BookCopy
Hold associates a Member with a Book (title) and sits in a per-title FIFO queue
Library has-a Catalog, a member registry, and a FineStrategy
BookCopy holds availability state, notified to Holds via Observer

design_patterns.where: Hold notification when a BookCopy becomes AVAILABLE
design_patterns.why: Decouple copy-return from notifying the next member in the hold queue; supports email/SMS observers.
Change fine policy without touching checkout/return.
Give clients one clean entry point over catalog/member/policy internals.

apis: void returnCopy(String copyBarcode) — computes fine, triggers next hold
Hold placeHold(String memberId, String isbn) / void cancelHold(holdId)
boolean renew(String loanId) — only if no active holds
state_transitions: BookCopy: AVAILABLE --checkout--> LOANED --return, holds waiting--> ON_HOLD --claimed by next member--> LOANED; ON_HOLD --hold expires--> AVAILABLE; any --reported lost--> LOST
Loan: ACTIVE --return on time--> RETURNED; ACTIVE --past due--> OVERDUE --return--> RETURNED (with fine)
Hold: WAITING --copy frees--> READY_FOR_PICKUP --claimed--> FULFILLED; WAITING/READY --cancel or expire--> CANCELLED
edge_cases: All copies out — offer a hold instead of checkout
Member at loan limit or with blocking overdue fines — reject checkout
Return of an overdue copy — compute fine, then route copy to next hold or make available
Hold queue ordering — strict FIFO; expired READY holds fall through to the next member
Lost copy — fine the member, mark LOST, remove from available count
Double return / returning a copy not on loan — idempotent guard
concurrency: Two members checking out the last available copy: allocate a specific BookCopy atomically (lock the copy row / compare-and-set its status) so only one succeeds
Copy freed with several waiting holds: fulfill the head of the FIFO queue atomically so two members aren't both offered the same copy
Fine computation and status transition on return must be atomic to avoid double-charging
Per-title hold queue guarded; member loan-count checks read-modify-write under a member lock
extensibility: New item types (DVD, e-book, magazine): introduce a LibraryItem base with BookCopy as one subtype; e-books skip physical copy/hold logic
New fine policy (grace period, tiered by tier): implement FineStrategy
Membership tiers with different limits: MembershipTier drives canBorrow and loan period
New notification channels: add NotificationObserver implementations
Digital lending with concurrent-license limits reuses the hold/queue concept

deep_dives.probe: Why separate Book from BookCopy? What breaks if you model availability and loans on Book directly when there are five physical copies?
A copy is returned and three members hold the title. Walk me through picking the next member and notifying them — where does Observer fit and how do you keep it FIFO and race-free?
Requirements change the fine from flat to tiered with a grace period. How does your design absorb that without editing checkout/return?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions copies or copy or availability
followup_bank.question: How do you model 'a title' vs 'a physical copy'? Where do loan state and availability live?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions hold or reserve or waitlist
followup_bank.question: When a copy is returned, how do you notify the next member fairly and without a race — Observer plus a FIFO queue?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions fine or fee or late
followup_bank.question: How do you support flat vs tiered vs capped fines without if/else scattered through return logic — a FineStrategy?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions dvd or ebook or media
followup_bank.question: How would you extend to non-book items without rewriting loans — a LibraryItem base type?
Two members grab the last copy at once — where exactly is the atomic allocation?

tradeoffs: Book/BookCopy split (correct, more classes) vs a single Book with a count (simpler, loses per-copy tracking) — the split is the right call
Observer notifications (decoupled, eventual) vs synchronous polling of holds
Strategy fine policy (flexible) vs inline calculation (simpler now)
Per-copy locking (fine-grained) vs a coarse library lock (simple, contended)
reference.reference_answer: A strong answer's first correct move is separating Book (bibliographic title) from BookCopy (a physical item with its own barcode and lifecycle) — loans and availability live on copies, not titles. Member/Account carries loan limits and fines; Loan links a member to a copy with due dates and computes overdue; Hold sits in a per-title FIFO queue. Copy and loan lifecycles are explicit state machines. Fine calculation is a Strategy (flat/tiered/capped), hold notification is an Observer fired when a returned copy has waiters, and a Repository/Catalog isolates search. The candidate handles all-copies-out (offer a hold), loan-limit/overdue blocking, lost copies, and double-return, and makes last-copy checkout and hold fulfillment atomic to avoid two members claiming the same copy. They show extensibility to DVDs/e-books via a LibraryItem base and to new fine/membership policies without touching checkout/return.

interviewer_notes: This looks like CRUD but has real OOD meat — the single biggest signal is the Book vs BookCopy distinction; if the candidate models loans/availability on Book directly, ask what happens with five copies and let them discover the split. Push the hold-fulfillment flow: FIFO queue plus Observer notification, and make them articulate the race when a returned copy has multiple waiters. Probe fine policy as a Strategy (requirements will 'change' to tiered-with-grace-period mid-interview to test open/closed). Check the copy/loan state machines are explicit, not implied by booleans. Concurrency focus: last-copy checkout and hold claim must be atomic. Over-engineering traps to flag: building a full search engine, a microservices split, or a payment gateway before the domain model is right. If time remains, the DVD/e-book extension tests whether the hierarchy is open for extension.
